clauses.reason: This clause, the whole of Executive Order 11013, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11013 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the maritime industry". The report deadline and standstill are spent facts recorded without an end date, and they did not end the order. The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03).

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (27 FR 3373) prints Executive Order 11013 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1962-04-07; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the maritime industry of the United States). I read the whole clause and the signature block. Inventory: the dossier's single whole-order clause covers the recitals and every operative sentence; nothing outside it is a command (any attached lists of carriers or unions identify parties and are not commands). The one operative clause creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 (29 U.S.C. 176) to inquire into the labor dispute described in the recitals, names its members, gives it the powers and duties of Title II of that Act, directs it to report to the President on or before the stated date, and provides that after its report the Board continues in existence to perform other functions required under the Act until the Board is terminated by the President. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11013 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the maritime industry". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The report date is a deadline, not an end. The order also makes the Board's continued existence last until the Board is terminated by the President. No held source records any presidential act terminating the Board before EO 12553, so that contingent own-terms ending is not evidenced; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 an unestablished earlier event is not claimed, and the express revocation is the first ending shown by held evidence. The unevidenced possibility of an earlier termination is disclosed as a point for the human reviewer. Earlier candidates: a search of the held order texts for citations of this order by number found no later order that revokes, amends or extends it; the Office of the Federal Register catalog notes name EO 12553 as the revoking order. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception, and the order created no continuing right or obligation outside its own terms. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

savings.reason: After a bounded search of the full text of EO 12553, the U.S. Code and eCFR (no hits for this order), and the Federal Register catalog notes, no savings clause, exception or surviving legal effect was found; EO 12553 revokes the order without any reservation.
